sources.said: Taking effect on Jan. 1, the 2026-2028 CMPA-DGC Standard Agreement establishes the terms, conditions and rates for directors and other professional crew members working in film, television and digital media productions in Canada, excluding B.C. and Quebec. … The new Standard Agreement will apply to productions commencing principal photography on or after Jan. 1, 2026. The agreement expires on Dec. 31, 2028.

figures.finding: In B.C. the DGC B.C. District Council collective agreement runs 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2028 with compounded general wage increases of 5.5%, 4% (29 March 2026) and 3.5% (4 April 2027); its director cutting time for long-form TV was sent to a joint Director Cut Committee.

These increases shall be compounded.

figures.finding: Canadian features are made mostly in English: of C$460M of theatrical feature production in 2024/25, English-language work was C$320M and French-language C$140M.
figures.applies: Canadian theatrical feature film production (CAVCO data), 2024/25.

sources.said: Overall, the volume of production declined by 3.2% from $475 million in 2023/24 to $460 million in 2024/25. French-language production increased by 35% to $140 million, while English-language production decreased by 13.8% to $320 million.

figures.finding: Ontario (Toronto) leads: Ontario-based producers made 52% of Canadian feature production in 2024/25, and across all film and television production Ontario took 36.3% of 2023 industry revenue, British Columbia 34.1% and Quebec 22.7%.
figures.applies: Canada; feature share by producer's province (CMPA) and industry operating revenue by province (Statistics Canada, 2023). The sources name provinces, not cities.

sources.said: Ontario-based producers accounted for the largest share (52%) of film production in 2024/25, with $238 million in production volume, followed by Quebec ($172 million), British Columbia ($34 million), Atlantic Canada ($11 million) and the Prairie Provinces and Territories ($5 million).
Industry revenue remained largely concentrated in 2023, with the vast majority of total industry revenue coming from Ontario (36.3%), British Columbia (34.1%) and Quebec (22.7%).
